summary: Entire file is dead code -- no function from jikan.functions.ts is imported anywhere in the active codebase (all callers import from anilist.functions.ts instead)
failure_scenario: ~250 lines of maintained, rate-limited API code that can never be reached, wasting bundle size and confusing future readers about which anime API is canonical

summary: Promise.allSettled delays showing any search results until the slowest API (TMDB or Anilist) responds, hiding fast API results
failure_scenario: A user searching on a slow network sees an empty loading skeleton for the full duration of the slowest API call, even though results from the faster API were ready seconds earlier

summary: isFetching shows only a spinner icon with no partial results, giving no feedback about which result sections are loading
failure_scenario: A user sees only a spinning loader for several seconds because Anilist is slow but TMDB results are immediately available, with no indication that some data has arrived

summary: listSeasonsWithProgress fetches ALL user_seasons rows for the entire user instead of filtering by the relevant season IDs
failure_scenario: A user with 100+ season entries across their library pays O(n) bandwidth and processing cost on every media detail page load even though only 5-20 season IDs are relevant to the current page

summary: Catch blocks in searchAll, trending, and discover check !process.env.TMDB_API_KEY to decide if the error is a config issue, but this is false when TMDB_READ_TOKEN is set without TMDB_API_KEY
failure_scenario: A user who configured TMDB_READ_TOKEN but not TMDB_API_KEY sees 'TMDB_API_KEY is not configured' on a real network failure, misleading them into thinking their config is wrong when it is the network that failed

summary: Same misleading check pattern in trending() catch block, repeated identically
failure_scenario: Same as above; the misleading config-wrong message surfaces in discover and trending sections too

summary: franchiseStatusesQ fires a Supabase query on every anime page load even when the current anime has no related franchise items (query is always enabled when isAnime and currentUserId are truthy via the enabled: !!id clause)
failure_scenario: For anime with no relations (e.g., a standalone film), a pointless Supabase query hits the database every page load, adding ~50-200ms of latency for zero benefit

summary: getUser(token) makes an HTTP request to Supabase Auth on every authenticated server function call, replacing the local JWT decode from the deprecated getClaims()
failure_scenario: Every authenticated server function (library CRUD, friends, reviews, activity) pays an extra ~100-300ms HTTP round-trip to Supabase Auth, compounding latency on pages that issue multiple server functions

summary: claims object is reduced to { sub: data.user.id }, silently discarding any other JWT claims (app_metadata, roles, custom claims) that downstream code might need
failure_scenario: Future code that reads context.claims.role or context.claims.app_metadata for authorization checks will get undefined and silently misbehave, since only sub is preserved

summary: Auto-complete series logic in setSeasonStatus makes 2 extra queries (all seasons, all season progress) on every season status update and uses app-level conditions instead of a database trigger
failure_scenario: Every click on a season status button triggers 2-3 additional database queries, and the auto-complete rule is easily bypassed by any future code path that updates season status outside setSeasonStatus

summary: removeLibraryItem deletes related user_seasons rows via app-level code in a silent try/catch block instead of using ON DELETE CASCADE at the schema level
failure_scenario: If the separate season-cleanup DELETE silently fails (caught by empty catch), orphaned user_seasons rows accumulate over time. Also, .maybeSingle() mangles the response expectation for multi-row deletes

summary: handleStatusChange contains hardcoded business logic redirecting 'planned' clicks to the first franchise item instead of the current media, coupling a UX policy to a React component
failure_scenario: If the same 'planned redirect' rule is ever needed from a different entry point (e.g., batch import, API endpoint, library bulk actions), it must be duplicated or the component refactored, violating DRY

summary: The franchise redirect depends on franchiseList[0] order (sorted by year then mal_id), which is an implicit fragile contract between a sorting memo and a click handler
failure_scenario: A future developer adjusts the sort order in the franchiseList useMemo for display purposes, unintentionally changing which item gets the 'planned' click, breaking the intended UX without any type error

summary: lovableOauthCompatibilityPlugin is a middleware shim that could be replaced by updating Supabase OAuth redirect URLs directly
failure_scenario: New developers must understand this plugin exists and its purpose; if forgotten, OAuth callbacks from other environments (mobile, API clients) will hit dead routes instead of /auth
